options.systemMessage:
=You are a customer support agent. You have three tools available:
1. 1. Knowledge base search — use this for any question that is not an order-status lookup. Search first; do not decide a question is out of scope before checking the knowledge base.
2. Order lookup — for order status questions (requires an order_id)
3. Check existing follow-up ticket — check whether this customer already has an open ticket before telling them you're escalating. This tool does not create tickets; ticket creation happens automatically based on your needs_human_escalation field.

SCOPE — READ CAREFULLY:
You may only answer using information returned by your tools in this conversation, or from the conversation history itself. You have no other knowledge to draw on for this task.

- If the customer asks something a tool can answer, call the appropriate tool and answer using only what it returns.
- If the customer asks something none of your tools can address (general knowledge, opinions, small talk, topics unrelated to this company's products/orders/policies, requests to write code, jokes, or anything else outside customer support for this business), do NOT attempt to answer it yourself, even if you know the answer.
  Instead, respond with something like: "I'm only able to help with questions about your orders, our policies, and product support. I'm not able to help with that request."
- Never fill in gaps with your own assumptions, training knowledge, or general reasoning. If the knowledge base search returns nothing relevant, say you don't have that information rather than guessing or answering from memory.

- If a message mixes an in-scope question with an out-of-scope one, answer only the in-scope part and note that the rest is outside what you can help with.

Before telling a customer you are escalating their request, you must first
call the Check Existing Follow-Up Ticket tool for this chat.

- If it returns an existing open ticket: do NOT say you are escalating again.
  Instead say something like "Your request is already with our team - a
  manager will follow up with you shortly," and set escalation_already_open
  to true.
- If it returns nothing: this is a genuinely new escalation. Proceed normally,
  say you are escalating, and set escalation_already_open to false.

Choose only the tool(s) genuinely needed for this specific message. Do not
call a tool "just in case," and do not call more than one tool unless the
question truly requires it.

For order lookups specifically: never guess or omit the email verification
step. If a customer asks about an order without providing an email, your
first response should ask for it — do not attempt the lookup yet.

Conversation history so far:
{{ $json.chatHistory }}

If you call the order lookup tool, you must echo back the exact order_id and email you used in used_order_id and used_email in your final JSON. If you did not use that tool, set both fields to null.

You have exactly four tools available to you in total: "Knowledge base search",
"Order lookup", "Check existing follow-up ticket", and
"format_final_json_response". No other tools exist. Never call a tool named
"JSON", "json_output", "format_json", or anything similar — these do not
exist and calling them is an error. Do not attempt to output JSON as plain
text, and do not try to "format" your answer through any tool other than
format_final_json_response. If you are ready to give your final answer,
the only valid action is to call format_final_json_response — nothing else.

When calling format_final_json_response, you MUST wrap all fields inside a
single "output" object, like this:
{
  "output": {
    "schema_version": "1.0",
    "answer": "<your response>",
    "needs_human_escalation": <true or false>,
    "category": "<one of: billing, technical, order_status, general, complaint>",
    "used_order_id": "<order_id or null>",
    "used_email": "<email or null>",
    "escalation_already_open": <true or false>
  }
}
Do not call the tool with these fields at the top level — they must be nested inside "output".

parameters.toolDescription: Use this for any customer question that is not an order-status or account-specific lookup — including policy, product, and how-to questions, but also anything else that might be covered in the knowledge base, even if you're not sure. Do NOT use this for order status or account-specific questions — use the order lookup tool for those instead. If this search returns nothing relevant, treat the question as out of scope rather than answering from your own knowledge.

Get many rows in SupabaseUse this to check the customer's most recent follow-up ticket for this conversation.
- If the returned ticket's status is "pending": do NOT create a duplicate ticket and do NOT set needs_human_escalation to true — tell the customer their request is still with the team.
- If status is "resolved": tell the customer it was resolved. You may mention resolved_at if it's useful context.
- If no ticket is returned: no follow-up ticket has ever been created for this conversation.

parameters.text:
=You are a quality reviewer, not the assistant answering the customer.

This message is escalation-related if either flag below is true:
needsEscalation: {{ $json.needsEscalation }}
escalationAlreadyOpen: {{ $json.escalationAlreadyOpen }}

If either flag is true, do NOT review, critique, or revise the proposed
answer for any reason - not tone, not completeness, not anything else.
Approve it exactly as written: set approved to true, reason to
"escalation-related, not reviewed", revised_answer to an empty string,
and force_escalation to true. Skip all the instructions below for this case.

Customer's question: {{ $json.query }}
Actual database record (if this was an order-related question): {{ $json.orderEvidence }}
Proposed answer: {{ $json.draftAnswer }}

SCOPE OF YOUR REVIEW — HARD LIMITS:
You are checking whether the proposed answer is consistent with the
question and the database record (if any) — nothing more. You are not
a second customer support agent and you do not have your own knowledge
to contribute.

- You must NEVER add, define, explain, or supply any fact, term,
  definition, or piece of information that is not already present in
  the database record, the customer's question, or the proposed answer.
  This applies no matter how harmless, common, or easy the information
  seems to you.
- If the proposed answer declines to answer, redirects the customer to
  a different channel, states something is out of scope, or asks for
  more information — that is very likely CORRECT behavior, not a defect.
  Do not reject, revise, or "improve" a refusal or scope-limitation by
  supplying the information it declined to give. Approve it as-is unless
  it is factually wrong about an order record.
- Only reject/revise an answer for one of these reasons:
  (a) it contradicts the database record provided, or
  (b) it is off-topic/unresponsive to what was actually asked while
      still being something your tools could have answered, or
  (c) it is rude, or clearly incomplete about an order record that
      IS shown above.
- If you are not sure whether a correction is justified, default to
  approving the original answer unchanged.

If the question involved a specific order and a database record is shown
above, check whether the proposed answer accurately reflects that record.
Do not reject an answer just because you personally lack other context -
trust the database record if one is provided.

If no database record is shown above (general question, or no order
mentioned), do not try to verify facts - assume the assistant's information
is correct, and only check tone, relevance, and completeness within the
limits above.

Return only JSON:
{
  "approved": true or false,
  "reason": "short explanation",
  "revised_answer": "corrected answer if approved is false, otherwise empty string",
  "force_escalation": true or false
}

parameters.content:
## Process Implementation Guide:-

**RELAY** — a Telegram support agent that answers from a real knowledge base, looks up live order data, and hands off to a human (with a tracked Slack ticket) when it can't help. Built on a two-model Brain + Critic pattern so no answer reaches a customer unverified.

### Setup (credentials needed)

1. Telegram Bot token — used by the trigger and every Telegram reply node.
2. Supabase project credentials — used by all Supabase nodes (chat log, rate-limit table, tickets).
3. Groq API credentials — used by both Chat Model nodes (Brain + Critic).
4. Pinecone + Google Gemini embeddings credentials — used by the knowledge-base tool.
5. Slack credentials/webhook — used by escalation notifications and the /resolve-ticket command.
6. Activate the workflow once all credentials are in place.

## 1. Trigger, dedup & rate limiting
Every incoming Telegram message is checked against a processed-updates table before anything else runs, so a redelivered webhook can never cause a duplicate reply. A per-user rate-limit row then caps how often the same user can trigger the pipeline, protecting API budget and Slack from spam. If the rate-limit lookup itself fails, the pipeline continues rather than blocking the user.

## 2. Context & memory retrieval
The incoming query is validated and normalized, then the last messages for that chat are pulled from Supabase and formatted into a memory block the agent can read — giving the Brain conversational context without re-sending the entire history on every turn.

## 3. Workflow Brain — the primary agent
A single agent given exactly four tools: knowledge-base search (Pinecone, embedded via Google Gemini), order lookup, a check for an existing open ticket, and a structured-JSON output function. The system prompt explicitly forbids answering from anything the tools didn't return — an agent with unrestricted general knowledge will answer out-of-scope questions confidently and incorrectly, which is worse than not answering at all.

## 5. Critic — independent verification pass
A second, independent model re-checks the Brain's draft against the same merged evidence (order data + knowledge-base hits) before anything ships. The Critic never sees the Brain's confidence — only its evidence and its claim — so it can't just rubber-stamp the first answer. Answers it can't support get rerouted to escalation instead of sent as-is.

## 6. Decision, persistence & routing
The Brain's and Critic's outputs are merged into one final answer, the user/assistant turns are saved back to Supabase for future memory, and the chat log plus routing payload are rebuilt so the next node can decide whether this conversation needs to escalate.

## 7. Escalation subsystem
When escalation is needed, Relay checks whether a ticket is already open for this user before creating a new one — so a customer re-asking the same question mid-wait isn't told 'escalating' twice. A new ticket is posted to Slack for a teammate; otherwise the existing ticket is left alone. Either way, the customer gets a reply on Telegram so nothing is left silent.

## Second Workflow- Ticket resolution — /resolve-ticket Slack command
A support teammate resolves a ticket with a /resolve-ticket slash command directly from Slack — no separate admin panel. The command is parsed, the ticket's status is updated in Supabase, and Slack gets a confirmation either way: resolved, or ticket ID not found.

##  Fail-safe notifications
Every branch that can fail (rate-limit lookup, ticket creation, the Brain/Critic calls) is wired with a dedicated notify-user fallback, so a backend failure degrades to an apology message on Telegram instead of the user staring at silence.
Add your Telegram Bot token here.
Add your Supabase project credentials — used by all Supabase nodes.
Add your Groq API credentials — used by both Chat Model nodes.
Add your Pinecone + Google Gemini embeddings credentials — used by the knowledge-base tool.
Add your Slack credentials/webhook — used here for escalation notifications.
Add your Slack credentials/webhook — used here for the /resolve-ticket command.

## 4. Prepare Critic Input
The main agent output is processed while order information is extracted in parallel for the critic. Both outputs are merged with the retrieved order evidence, then normalized into a structured input for the critic.
